newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto sees Roundup Ready corn by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto sees Roundup Ready corn by 1998.

text.p: U.S. chemicals group Monsanto Co said it expects to license production of a genetically altered type of corn that thrives with its popular herbicide Roundup in time for the 1998 U.S. crop year.
"We look to have Roundup Ready corn available for commercial application as early as 1998," Monsanto spokesman Loren Wassell said.

The U.S. Agriculture Department on Wednesday opened a 60-day public comment period based on a petition by Monsanto to produce a corn line, MON 802, developed to tolerate Roundup and repel the European corn borer, a crop pest.
The European Commission on Wednesday approved the sale of genetically altered corn as food or seed in its member countries, a step welcomed by USDA Secretary Dan Glickman.

The U.S. approved commercial use of genetically altered corn months ago. Corn genetically engineered to produce a biopesticide that repels corn borers was planted on about 0.5 percent of U.S. acreage this year.

Monsanto's powerful Roundup herbicide is widely used in U.S. agriculture. A type of "Roundup-Ready" soybeans developed by Monsanto and planted this year prompted widespread consumer protests in Europe led by the environmental group Greenpeace.
